title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 22 Jun to 26 Sep 2026
summary: Over 96 days, from 22 Jun to 26 Sep 2026, the radar shows the lake shrinking from 31.35 km2 to 29.82 km2, or -4.9%. The land around it barely changed: only 0.88 km2 turned brighter in HV.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: The lake lost 1.53 km2. In HV, 0.88 km2 became brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.42 km2 darker, and mean HV moved by 0.05 dB. HH rose more, by 0.46 dB on average, with 3.12 km2 brighter.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: Trees, shrub and rugged slopes, 192.98 km2, had only 0.3 km2 brighter in HV. On the open water type, 0.87 km2 turned brighter in HH, which fits a shoreline that moved: ground left dry by falling water echoes more than water does.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause: summer drawdown for irrigation and evaporation; the dam's level and release records would confirm it. Possible cause: some method noise, since 11.5% and 9.2% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo; a shoreline survey would measure it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Compare the 1.53 km2 loss with the dam's level readings to turn area into volume. Follow the lake every 12 days through the irrigation season, since the Beni Moussa canals that ORMVAT plans to modernise draw on it.
